narrative: In the 2020s, Black and African women's hairstyles continue to be a vibrant reflection of their rich cultural heritage. The natural hair movement remains strong, encouraging individuals to celebrate their afro-textured locks in all their glory. Styles like the afro, cornrows, and box braids are still widely popular, with many embracing these traditional looks as a way to connect with their African roots. Dreadlocks and locs also remain a staple in some communities, while protective hairstyles like Bantu knots continue to be celebrated for their ability to minimize hair breakage. While the 2020s may not have been extensively documented in terms of Black and African women's hairstyles, it is clear that these styles remain an integral part of their identity and culture. As a testament to this, we see a continued emphasis on embracing natural textures and traditional braiding practices, with many individuals proudly showcasing their unique styles as a celebration of their heritage.
